initial.question: Characterize ordinary oriented unframed closures using only even strand-state vertices, for classical and virtual braids.
ownDerivations: Define projection P on every unrestricted state by positive right stabilization only when m odd. P fixes even endpoints and preserves closures. Soundness verifies each displayed scheme as a path through permitted old moves. Completeness paces each unrestricted generator edge separately; defining relations at odd m extend in context with retained σ_m. Odd conjugation becomes BC; even becomes C. Stabilization from an even state becomes D with g on index m and positive tail m+1, from odd becomes T from old σ_m padding to g. Reverse edges covered.

For virtual exchanges the unshifted blocks on m−1 strands have indices <=m−2. At even total m right/left produce R/L. At odd m total N=m+1, padding σ_{N−1}; right local exchange index N−2 and block support <=N−3. Left shift applies only to blocks and exchanges at index1. Tail remains unshifted after virtual move. m=1 edge trivial because only empty word; exchanges need m>=2 and first odd m=3. This is a graph-image proof and needs exact primary generator definitions, above all possible Kamada exchange normalization and tags.

Maximum count identity uses monotone m↦m+(m mod 2), giving even ceil bound for a supplied certificate only. Ordinary vs plat identity two-strand example checks. Tags cannot be suppressed as empty words give n-component unlink. Fox3 color operator is unipotent with square-zero nilpotent part mod3, order3 and diagonal fixed locus, so overstated T support connects trefoil coloring 9 to unknot coloring3. Virtual omitted support makes σ1² vs (σ1 v1)² with resulting ordered signed crossing matrices (1,1) and (2,0) up to simultaneous relabel; detour adds no classical crossings.
Definitions retain arbitrary finite blocks, no claimed geometrically local/minimal scheme list. No firstness; Nencka inaccessible full texts cannot settle historical priority or override own theorem.

exact_scope: For ordinary oriented unframed classical and virtual closures, every nonempty link has an even representative. For any two even-tagged representatives, equivalent closures are equivalent under contextual defining relations and the listed four or eight reversible schemes, respectively. A supplied witness of height M converts with height at most 2 ceil(M/2).
root_mathematics: Positive right stabilization gives a closure-preserving projection from each odd tagged word onto the next even level, fixing all even states. At odd level a contextual relation retains the old word context and independent terminal crossing. The two parities of conjugation give C/BC; stabilization gives D/T; right exchange gives R/BR and shifted left exchange L/BL. Each lift unpacks into permitted original moves, proving soundness. At N=2 BC and exchange are trivial where applicable; one-strand identity pads to the unknot. Nontrivial even tags preserve distinct unlink component counts. Enlarging T fails by Fox 3-colorings; enlarging R fails by a signed ordered crossing matrix even though counts agree.

independent_adversary.name: even_markov_adversarial_sol
independent_adversary.findings: Exact parity retraction and contextual relation families, literal exchange signs and shift, low-strand support counterexamples, and the supplied height bound. Enlarging either BC block can change component count. Enlarging BR can change the ordered crossing matrix. BL is redundant using L and far commutations, consistent with the stated sufficient scheme list.
